This bead's premise -- that durability-gap recovery needs a genuine unbuilt
non-redelivery mechanism ("fix option 1 or 3") for the test to pass -- does
NOT hold. Investigation (production code reading + git archaeology) showed:

1. `fail_confirmations(3) == CONFIRM_PUBLISH_MAX_ATTEMPTS` exhausts every
   in-process retry attempt inside publish_confirmed_event_with_retry
   (crate/sinexd/src/event_engine/jetstream_consumer/confirmation.rs), which
   IS a real fatal path (is_fatal_batch_processing_error ->
   JetStreamConsumer::run() returns Err -> the consumer is tracked as a
   "critical task" in event_engine/service.rs and its death fails the whole
   critical-task set). This design tripwire is intentional per CLAUDE.md's
   documented pipeline stage "confirmed publish GATES the ack (durability
   gap = redelivery)": production recovery is via process restart (systemd
   Restart=on-failure) + JetStream redelivering the unacked raw message to a
   fresh consumer instance.

2. But that full-exhaustion/fatal/restart scenario is NOT what this specific
   test (jetstream_consumer_republishes_confirmed_event_without_raw_redelivery)
   is exercising, and never was after 2026-03-27. `git show 2322eb0d2` (PR
   #196) shows the test's assertion was DELIBERATELY changed at that time
   from `deliveries >= 2` (crash + raw redelivery) to `deliveries == 1`
   (in-process retry succeeds, no redelivery needed) when it was renamed
   from jetstream_consumer_redelivers_when_confirmation_publish_fails to
   jetstream_consumer_queues_durable_confirmation_retries_without_raw_redelivery.
   That rename encoded a real, working design: publish_confirmed_event_with_retry's
   in-process backoff-retry loop already recovers from partial failures
   without ever reaching the fatal path. The `fail_confirmations(3)` call-site
   argument was simply never updated to match the new assertion semantics --
   a plain off-by-one leftover from before the rename, not a hint that a
   missing recovery mechanism needs building.

3. This bead's design notes claimed "no reconciliation/backfill mechanism ...
   rationale not documented in commit body" -- true narrowly (the PR #196
   body doesn't explain the rename), but the diff itself makes the intent
   unambiguous once read directly.
